proposal_text:
SUPERSEDES the proposal VETOed at META_LEDGER entry #749, which supersedes the one VETOed at #748. Entry #749's six grounds are addressed below in its own order, and its central finding is accepted without argument: the previous proposal diagnosed that nothing keys on the audited scope and then keyed on the ledger phase number, which is a different thing. The phase-keyed N=4 detector is withdrawn entirely, along with the tightening of the phase-reference regex that only existed to serve it. Nothing in qor/scripts/veto_pattern.py changes, in body or in input.

(a) THE KEY, AND THE RECORD THAT PRODUCES IT. Not a ledger parse. Every audit already writes its own scope: .qor/gates/<session_id>/audit_history.jsonl carries a `target` field naming the audited plan path, present in all 1741 records across 188 session histories. The key is that field, normalised by replacing backslashes with forward slashes, counted within one session. No regex, no ledger read, no new parser, and no discrimination problem between plan tribunals and remediation tribunals, because a remediation proposal is a different `target` string.

Measured on that key: 192 distinct (session, target) scopes after normalisation. Entry #749's correction stands, and this is the corrected picture, not the phase-keyed one -- phase 223's nine ledger tribunals are two scopes here, the plan at five and docs/remediation-phase223-detector-blind-spots-2026-08-12.md at four, and the phase 223 plan reached five and still sealed.

(b) THE HOOK POINT, WHICH DETERMINES THE THRESHOLD. Add a third mode to qor/scripts/cycle_count_escalator.py alongside `check` and `check_session_total`, returning an EscalationRecommendation with escalation_reason="scope-count". It is surfaced where those two already are: /qor-audit Step 0.5 and /qor-plan Step 2c.

Step 0.5 runs, in the skill's own words, "before engaging adversarial mode", so the current audit's history record does not yet exist when the check runs. A threshold N therefore fires as attempt N+1 begins, leaving 4-N attempts against the five-attempt cap. N=3 leaves two. That is the property entry #749 showed no placement of N=4 can deliver, and it is the reason for choosing three here rather than an appeal to noise.

MEASURED AT N=3 ON THE SCOPE KEY, BOTH DIRECTIONS. Twelve of 192 scopes reach three or more: the phase 223 plan (5), 258 (5), 261 (5), 265 (5), the phase 223 remediation document (4), 248 (4), and 224, 249, 250, 251, 253 and 254 at three each. Three were abandoned at the cap (258, 261, 265); nine recovered and sealed. Nine false positives against three true ones is a poor ratio stated bare, and the previous proposal rejected N=3 on exactly that ratio. What changes the judgement is not the ratio but the price of being wrong, which the previous proposal never priced.

(c) WHAT A FIRING COSTS, STATED PLAINLY. No new Process Shadow Genome event is emitted. This is the substantive difference from the vetoed design: the existing escalator returns a recommendation for the operator, and emits nothing when it fires. The only genome cost arises on operator DECLINE, via the existing severity-2 orchestration_override event.

That cost is bounded only under a condition this proposal must state. check_shadow_threshold._signature falls back to a digest of the whole details blob when no `gate`, `capability` or `pattern` key is present, and orchestration_override.record puts `reason` into details. A FIXED reason string therefore collapses every decline to one signature and one severity-2 contribution in total; an interpolated one does not, and /qor-plan already passes interpolated reasons such as f"user override: {result.errors}" which never collapse. This proposal requires the literal, uninterpolated reason "scope-count escalation declined".

DEPENDENCY, AND IT IS BLOCKING. The decline-once story is currently false for the mode this would resemble. cycle_count_escalator.check_session_total calls _suppression_active(session_id, None), and that helper returns False whenever first_match_ts is None, so the suppression marker is never read and a declined cumulative escalation re-fires on the next audit in the same session. Its docstring claims the opposite. Filed as GH #447. Until #447 is fixed, nine false-positive scopes would nag on every subsequent audit and each decline would append another event, so this proposal is not implementable ahead of it. The scope mode must pass a real timestamp -- the oldest audit record contributing to the over-threshold scope -- and its closure tests must assert that a marker written after that timestamp suppresses.

(d) CLOSURE ENFORCER: tests/test_cycle_count_escalator.py. It gains: a test that the scope mode fires at three and not at two, built from synthetic audit records; a test that `docs\plan.md` and `docs/plan.md` count as one scope, built from the real drift described below; a test that a decline recorded after the oldest contributing record suppresses the next check and one recorded before it does not, which is the GH #447 behaviour and fails today; and a live binding that asserts an INVARIANT rather than a set -- every scope the mode reports has a normalised count of at least three, and every scope with a count of at least three is reported. Entry #749 ruled the exact-firing-set form inadmissible under doctrine-test-discipline.md line 35, and it is not used. The unbounded "does not alter any other result for any input" test is also dropped; in its place, a test that the existing `check` and `check_session_total` return values are byte-identical before and after, on the fixture corpus those two already own.

(e) THE MEASURED DEFECTS OF THIS ROUTE, DISCLOSED BY NAME RATHER THAN DISCOVERED LATER. First, `target` format drifts: seven records from phases 101 through 107 carry a prose title such as "Phase 101: PyPI Publication Hardening P0 (GH #118 partial)" rather than a path, and seven carry Windows separators, with phases 217 and 218 each split across both separator forms inside a single session. Normalisation merges the separator split; the seven prose titles remain distinct keys at count one each and are harmless at any threshold, but they mean the key is not guaranteed to be a path. Second, a synthetic fixture directory sess-12345 holds 494 records against docs/plan-qor-phaseXX.md; session-scoped reading dissolves this entirely, because the mode reads .qor/gates/<current_sid>/ and never globs .qor/gates/*, and the closure tests must not glob either. Third, a session-scoped counter cannot see a scope audited across two sessions, which phase 225 was; its two records are one per session, so no threshold would have fired on it in any case, but the blindness is real and is the accepted cost of not globbing.

DOCTRINE HALF, unchanged and untouched by both verdicts, standing on entries #743 through #747: a characterization corpus offered as a behaviour-preserving refactor's safety argument must be derived from the code's acceptance conditions rather than enumerated by the author.

PROCESS FINDING FOR THE RECORD. Entry #749 disclosed that the tribunal seeded the defect it vetoed -- entry #748 wrote that parse_in_flight_audit_count "already computes exactly that", meaning audit count per plan path, and it does not. Two proposals were written to an instruction that was wrong. The countermeasure is not more careful proposal-writing: it is that a tribunal's Required Next Action, when it names a function as already computing something, is a claim like any other and must be executed before it is written.
supersedes: the proposal VETOed at META_LEDGER entry #749
